questions.statement: In the Text V, the author refers to several scholars and organizations, such as Knobel and Lankshear (2014), Kern (2000), the New London Group (1996), and others. What is the author's main purpose in including these references throughout the text?

options.text: To criticize traditional views of literacy and discredit the contributions of scholars who support outdated educational models.
To contrast different definitions of literacy and show the inconsistency among current theorists.
To demonstrate that there is no consensus on what literacy means, highlighting the confusion in educational theory.
To question the relevance of literacy in contemporary education and propose a return to basic reading and writing skills.
To provide credibility and support for the perspective that literacy is a dynamic, multidimensional concept rooted in sociocultural practices.

questions.explanation: As referências a pesquisadores e grupos teóricos fundamentam a argumentação e conferem credibilidade à concepção sociocultural e multidimensional de letramento. Elas não pretendem rejeitar os estudos citados, negar a relevância do tema ou defender ensino mecânico.

questions.statement: Contextual clues such as definitions, examples, modifiers, relocation, parallel structures, connectors, and the repetition of keywords play a vital role in enhancing the flow and clarity of academic texts. In the Text V, the term 'however', present in the following excerpt, is used as one of these contextual clues. About it, select the correct alternative. “An emphasis on the development of literacy as a fluid concept (Knobel and Lankshear (2014) is one of the most recent advances in twenty-first-century education. To conceptualize literacy, the ability of the learner to make use of language takes precedence in typical Western educational systems. However, as Kern highlights, “literacy is more than a set of academic skills” (2000, 23). It varies depending on the social context and is embedded in cultural practice (Paesani et al. 2016).”

options.text: “However” functions as a connector to introduce a supporting point that aligns with previous arguments and could be replaced by “additionally”.
“However” is used to introduce a contrasting point that deviates from the previous discussion and could be effectively replaced by “nevertheless”.
“However” serves to summarize the information presented, leading to a conclusion and could be substituted with “in conclusion”.
“However” provides an elaboration on a specific detail mentioned earlier and could be replaced by “specifically”.
“However” is utilized to emphasize a repeated keyword for clarity and could be substituted by “namely”.

questions.explanation: 'However' introduz contraste entre uma concepção mais instrumental de letramento e a visão ampliada defendida na citação. 'Nevertheless' preserva essa relação adversativa; conectores de adição, conclusão, especificação ou reformulação não reproduzem o sentido.

questions.statement: In relation to the term “whose” in the sentence: “We define literacy as a dynamic and multidimensional concept whose main aim is to provide twenty-first-century learners with the language skills [...]”, select the correct alternative.

options.text: “Whose” acts as a conjunction that links two independent clauses.
“Whose” functions as a relative pronoun that connects the concept to its main aim.
“Whose” serves as an interjection to add emphasis to the sentence.
“Whose” is used as a preposition to indicate direction.
“Whose” is used as a reflexive pronoun to emphasize the subject.

questions.explanation: 'Whose' é pronome relativo possessivo: retoma 'concept' e estabelece a relação entre o conceito de letramento e seu objetivo principal. Não une orações independentes como conjunção, nem exerce função de interjeição, preposição direcional ou pronome reflexivo.
